kata.name: Rule lens near-floor negative control (kata-6 triviality-floor analog)
kata.series_report: openspec/changes/add-rule-lens/design.md Decision 4 (pre-registered negative control; no prior series run)
kata.series_verdict: killed (pre-registered: at the 3-rule/4-input floor the conventional 4-row check catches every injected fault; the lens buys zero unique detections)

expected.detail: remove the trivial `basic` rule; the (basic, member=false) input is a gap -> underconstraint (hypothesized)
widen `member` to member OR tier=gold and move it first; `gold` is dead -> redundant (shadow)
declare `DeclaredDisjoint` on the overlapping trivial table -> pairwise violations

commands: cargo run -p catherine-cli -- rules fixtures/rule_lens/kata/negative-control/near-floor.ct.json rules --values tier=basic,gold --values member=true,false --json  # exit 0, findings []

cargo run -p catherine-cli -- rules fixtures/rule_lens/kata/negative-control/faults/01-gap-remove-basic.ct.json rules --values tier=basic,gold --values member=true,false --json  # exit 6, 1 finding(s) [gap]

cargo run -p catherine-cli -- rules fixtures/rule_lens/kata/negative-control/faults/02-shadow-widen-member.ct.json rules --values tier=basic,gold --values member=true,false --json  # exit 7, 1 finding(s) [shadow]

cargo run -p catherine-cli -- rules fixtures/rule_lens/kata/negative-control/faults/03-overlap-policy-swap.ct.json rules --values tier=basic,gold --values member=true,false --json  # exit 3, 2 finding(s) [overlap]

witness.question: which action applies? no rule covers this input class

comparison.conventional_baseline: prototype/rule_lens_baseline.py --kata near-floor: 4 frozen one-line assertions, one per input of the trivial table. Catches all 3 injected faults (3/3); zero unique detections for the lens.

expressibility_gap.invariant: three-factor derivability: R_k = R_i AND R_j AND R_l
expressibility_gap.why: the analysis checks exactly two combining factors; a three-rule derivation is not reported at any table size

discrepancies: Control scope: the injected near-floor faults are behavior-changing (the kata-6 analog). A behavior-preserving duplicate/subsumed rule would be lens-only even at this floor, so the zero-unique result is scoped to faults that change an asserted action, not a claim that structural redundancy is undetectable.
procedure: 1. Build the trivial 3-rule table over the 4-input domain (tier in {basic,gold} x member in {true,false}); `catherine rules` reports 0 findings.
2. Freeze the conventional 4-row check (one assertion per input) before injecting faults.
3. Inject 3 behavior-changing faults: remove `basic` (gap), widen `member` and move it first (shadow), declare `DeclaredDisjoint` (overlap).
4. Run the conventional check and `catherine rules` on each variant; count unique detections (lens caught AND baseline missed).
5. Zero unique detections -> the control self-negates: verdict killed, no advantage at the floor.
